intro:
Use it for the tools of an editor: a drawing canvas, a photo editor, a video timeline. It holds two kinds of control. A `Toolbar.Tool` is a mode, such as the pen or the select tool; exactly one in its `Toolbar.Group` is on until another is chosen. A `Toolbar.Button` is an action, such as undo, that does its job and leaves nothing on.

Give every tool and button a `label`. The buttons show only icons, so the label is their tooltip and what a screen reader reads.

For a few views of one panel, use [Tabs](/docs/web/components/tabs). For buttons that act on one thing together, such as a split button, use [Button Group](/docs/web/components/button-group).
usage:
<Toolbar>
  <Toolbar.Group defaultValue="select" aria-label="Tools">
    <Toolbar.Tool value="select" label="Select" shortcut="V">
      <MousePointer2Icon />
    </Toolbar.Tool>
    <Toolbar.Tool value="pen" label="Pen" shortcut="P">
      <PenToolIcon />
    </Toolbar.Tool>
  </Toolbar.Group>
  <Toolbar.Separator />
  <Toolbar.Button label="Undo" shortcut="⌘Z" onClick={undo}>
    <Undo2Icon />
  </Toolbar.Button>
</Toolbar>

parts.Group: Tools of which exactly one is on. `value` and `onValueChange`, or `defaultValue`, hold which one, by its `value`. Choosing the tool that is already on leaves it on. A filled marker in the primary colour sits under the chosen tool and glides to the next one.
parts.Tool: One tool in a group. `label` is its tooltip and its name for a screen reader, and `shortcut` shows its key in the tooltip.
parts.Button: An action: undo, zoom, export. `label` and `shortcut` work as on a tool. `render` makes another trigger the button, such as a `Menu.Trigger`, so a menu opens from the strip.
parts.Separator: A short line between sets of controls that belong apart, such as the tools and the history buttons.
parts.Caret: A small chevron saying a button opens more choices. Beside an icon it marks that button; alone in a `Toolbar.Button`, it makes that button a slim chevron against the tool before it, which turns over while its menu is open.

examples.title: A rail
examples.description: `orientation="vertical"` stands the strip up beside a canvas. The marker moves up and down, the arrow keys follow the column, and tooltips open to the side.

examples.title: A tool with options
examples.description: A `Toolbar.Button` holding only a `Toolbar.Caret` is drawn as a slim chevron against the tool before it. Rendered as a `Menu.Trigger`, it opens the shapes the tool can draw, and the chevron turns over while the menu is open. The tool then shows the shape last chosen and draws it.

examples.title: History and zoom
examples.description: Actions sit beside other controls in the same strip. Here a `line` [Slider](/docs/web/components/slider) zooms, each zoom the hand settles on is a step of history, and undo and redo are disabled at either end of it.

examples.title: Shortcuts
examples.description: With `shortcuts` on, a tool's single-key `shortcut` chooses it from anywhere on the page. Keys typed into a field, and keys pressed with ⌘, Ctrl or Alt, are left alone. Turn it on for the one toolbar that owns the page.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `sm`, `md` and `lg` set the size of every button and icon in the strip, and the corners and padding with them.

notes:
### Keyboard

The strip is one stop in the tab order. The arrow keys move along it, Home and End go to its ends, and Space or Enter chooses a tool or presses a button.

A `shortcut` written as one key, such as `V`, is answered when `shortcuts` is on. One written with a modifier, such as `⌘Z`, is only shown in the tooltip; handle that key yourself, because the page may already use it.

### Floating or inline

`floating`, the default, draws the strip on a raised surface of its own, for a strip laid over a canvas. `inline` draws the buttons only, for a strip inside a header or a panel that already has a surface.

With reduced motion turned on, the marker moves to the chosen tool without gliding.
